newsitem.title: USA: Wisconsin becomes 21st state to sue tobacco firms.
newsitem.headline: Wisconsin becomes 21st state to sue tobacco firms.

text.p: Wisconsin filed suit against the tobacco industry Wednesday, becoming the 21st state to take legal action against the manufacturers and promoters of cigarettes and chewing tobacco.

Following through on a promise made in November, state Attorney General James Doyle said Wisconsin sought to recoup money it has spent on health care costs attributable to tobacco and to force the industry to transform its marketing strategy.
"With 21 states now in the fight, the battle against the tobacco companies today has come of age," Doyle said in a statement regarding the suit filed in Dane County Circuit Court in Madison.
Philip Morris Cos. Inc. which was among the companies named in the suit, branded the action "baseless."

"These types of suits are fatally flawed, factually and legally, and we believe that ultimately the state will lose -- after spending millions of taxpayer dollars in time and costs," Gregory Little, senior assistant general counsel for Philip Morris, said in a statement.
Little also said that in 1996, sales of cigarettes generated more than $198 million in excise taxes alone for Wisconsin.

A spokesman for R.J. Reynolds, also named in the suit, said the company was preparing a statement, but had no immediate comment. Cigarette makers have consistently responded to such suits by saying they were without merit.

In a seperate development involving R.J. Reynolds, a Kansas magistrate has ordered the cigarette maker to produce documents in a civil suit that could show it knew since the 1950s that nicotine was addictive and caused serious health problems.

Wisconsin's 124-page complaint charged the tobacco industry engaged in a conspiracy to "mislead, deceive and confuse Wisconsin residents about the health effects of tobacco use and the addictiveness of nicotine." The suit demanded the industry disclose its "secret research" on the harmful effects of tobacco and nicotine.
Late last month, New York filed a similar suit, noting that private insurance companies and the state's Medicaid programme spent $2.6 billion yearly treating smoking-related illnesses.

The filing of the state lawsuits comes as Brooke Group Ltd. Chairman Bennett LeBow is seeking a settlement with all states that have filed Medicaid lawsuits against tobacco makers. Brooke's subsidiary is the first tobacco company to ever settle cigarette lawsuits.
In addition, some state attorneys general and some plaintiffs lawyers also are seeking a possible legislative solution to the mounting litigation against the industry.

The defendants named in the suit included R.J. Reynolds Tobacco, a division of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp.; Philip Morris; Brown and Williamson Tobacco Corp., which is owned by B.A.T Industries Plc; Loews Corp.'s Lorillard Tobacco Co.; Brooke Group Ltd.'s Liggett Group Inc. and UST Inc.'s United States Tobacco Co.
Also named in the suit was New York public relations firm Hill & Knowlton, Inc.; The Council for Tobacco Research - U.S.A., Inc.; The Tobacco Institute, Inc.; and The Smokeless Tobacco Council, Inc.
